messages.dashlet.topflows.bytes.tooltip: Top 10 flows by total bytes, including protocol, local and remote IP addresses, download and upload rates, total bytes, and remote ASN.
messages.dashlet.top10.downloaders.tooltip: Top 10 Downloaders by bits per second, including IP address, download and upload rates, round-trip time, TCP retransmits, and shaping plan.
messages.dashlet.worst10.rtt.tooltip: Worst 10 Downloaders by round-trip time, including IP address, download and upload rates, round-trip time, TCP retransmits, and shaping plan.
messages.dashlet.worst10.retransmits.tooltip: Worst 10 Downloaders by TCP retransmits, including IP address, download and upload rates, round-trip time, TCP retransmits, and shaping plan.
messages.dashlet.top10.uploaders.tooltip: Top 10 Uploaders by bits per second, including IP address, download and upload rates, round-trip time, TCP retransmits, and shaping plan.
messages.dashlet.topflows.rate.tooltip: Top 10 flows by rate, including protocol, local and remote IP addresses, download and upload rates, total bytes, and remote ASN.
messages.dashlet.top10.downloads_graphic.tooltip: The top-10 users by bits-per-second. The ribbon goes red as they approach capacity. The name border indicates round-trip time, while the main label color indicates TCP retransmits. The legend is current download speed, followed by number of retransmits.
messages.dashlet.top10.uploads_graphic.tooltip: The top-10 users by bits-per-second. The ribbon goes red as they approach capacity. The name border indicates round-trip time, while the main label color indicates TCP retransmits. The legend is current upload speed, followed by number of retransmits.
messages.dashlet.country.tooltip: Top 10 endpoints by country/region, ordered by download speed. This data is gathered from recently completed flows, and may be a little behind realtime.
messages.dashlet.ether_protocols.tooltip: Bytes and packets transferred over IPv4 and IPv6, and the round-trip time for each. This data is gathered from recently completed flows, and may be a little behind realtime.
messages.dashlet.ip_protocols.tooltip: Bytes transferred over TCP/UDP/ICMP and port numbers, matched to common services when possible. This data is gathered from recently completed flows, and may be a little behind realtime.
messages.dashlet.cpu.tooltip: Percentage of CPU time spent on user processes, system processes, and idle time. This includes both LibreQoS and anything else running on the server.
messages.dashlet.ram.tooltip: Percentage of RAM used and free. This includes both LibreQoS and anything else running on the server.
messages.dashlet.flow_duration.tooltip: How long do flows last in seconds? Most flows are very short, while some can last a very long time.
messages.dashlet.rtt_histo3d.tooltip: Round-Trip Time Histogram, expanded to include time as a third dimension. This can be helpful for seeing how your performance is changing over time.

messages.dashlet.capacity.circuits.title: Circuits At Capacity
messages.dashlet.capacity.circuits.tooltip: Customer circuits using close to their maximum capacities, and possibly in need of an upsell.
messages.dashlet.capacity.tree.title: Tree Nodes At Capacity
messages.dashlet.capacity.tree.tooltip: Distribution Nodes approaching their maximum capacity, possibly in need of an upgrade or a better shaping policy.
messages.dashlet.queue_dynamics.tooltip: Live global queue dynamics on a 30-second window. Top panel: the delivered (shaped) throughput with the configured capacity line, plus the offered/demand rate where the box reports one — on a bridge box the demand is zero until the backend ships it, otherwise the demand line is omitted. Bottom panel: the global host-median round-trip time from the bridge RTT histogram.
messages.dashlet.mapped.tooltip: Shows the amount of traffic that is mapped (shaped) and unmapped. Mapped traffic follows configured bandwidth limits; unmapped traffic is not.
messages.dashlet.pps.tooltip: Shows the current throughput in packets per second. Traffic is divided between upload (from the ISP) and download (to the ISP) traffic.
messages.dashlet.stormguard_bandwidth.tooltip: Real-time visualization of bandwidth limits for monitored sites over the last 5 minutes. Shows download bandwidth (solid lines above zero) and upload bandwidth (dashed lines below zero) for each site.
messages.dashlet.stormguard_bandwidth.caption: Live StormGuard queue limits
messages.dashlet.tracked_flows.tooltip: Number of flows tracked by LibreQoS. Flows are either a TCP connection, or a UDP/ICMP connection with matching endpoints and port/request type numbers. Completed flows are flows that have finished transmitting data, and have been submitted to netflow and the flow analysis system.
messages.dashlet.rtt_histo.tooltip: Round-Trip Time Histogram, showing the distribution of round-trip times for packets in real-time.
messages.dashlet.lts_24h.heading: 24 Hour Throughput
messages.dashlet.lts_24h.tooltip: Throughput for the last 24 hours. The error bars indicate minimum and maximum within a time range, while the points indicate median. Many other systems will inadvertently give incorrect data by averaging across large periods of time, and not sampling frequently enough (1 second for Mb/s).
messages.dashlet.lts_shaper_status.heading: Shaper Status
messages.dashlet.lts_shaper_status.tooltip: Status from each of the LibreQoS shapers you are running.
messages.dashlet.cake_stats.tooltip: Total number of fair queueing interventions per second. ECN Marks label packets as having possible congestion, signalling the flow to slow down. Drops discard selected packets to "pace" the queue for efficient, fair, low-latency throughput.
messages.dashlet.retransmits.tooltip: TCP retransmits over time. Retransmits can happen because CAKE is adjusting packet pacing, but large volumes are often indicative of a network problem - particularly customer Wi-Fi problems.
messages.circuit.rate.assigned_effective_tooltip: Assigned max {assigned} Mbps; effective queue max {effective} Mbps
messages.circuit.rate.assigned_effective_aria: Assigned max {assigned} Mbps. Effective queue max {effective} Mbps.

messages.trial.teaser.issue_triage.title: Issue Triage
messages.trial.teaser.issue_triage.body: Turn symptoms into a focused troubleshooting summary with likely causes and recommended next steps.
messages.trial.teaser.api_only.title: API-Only Option
messages.trial.teaser.api_only.body: Choose the lower-cost API-only option when you only need provisioning and automation integrations. Hosted dashboards and remote Insight history are not included.
messages.sponsor.message.shaping_history: LibreQoS handles shaping. Insight adds history, dashboards, and alerts so you catch issues before tickets arrive.
messages.sponsor.message.proof: Need proof before or after changes? Insight keeps latency, retransmit, and flow history in one place.
messages.sponsor.message.heatmaps: Insight heatmaps make congestion trends obvious across sites and APs. Find busy hours fast.
messages.sponsor.message.multiple_shapers: Managing multiple shapers? Insight gives you one dashboard view across locations.
messages.sponsor.message.ai_reports: Insight AI reports summarize what changed and where to look first, cutting troubleshooting time.
messages.sponsor.message.slow_internet: When customers say internet is slow, Insight helps you verify latency, retransmits, and utilization fast.
messages.sponsor.message.visibility: LibreQoS handles shaping. Insight adds visibility, trends, and alerts so you can run ops proactively.
messages.sponsor.message.historical_context: See circuit and site behavior over time, not just right now. Insight gives you historical context.
